title: Sessionless streaming compatibility SDK patterns for multi-language tool invocation
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: provide a compact, sessionless compatibility layer across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs that maps the new framed streaming protocol (event envelopes) to common developer ergonomics: TypeScript EventEmitter / callback streams, Python async generators, and Go channels. The layer must: 1) preserve structured outputs (JSON fragments / tool call records), 2) reconcile tool/function call lifecycle (invocation, confirmation, result), 3) offer backward-compatible adapters for generator-based legacy SDKs, and 4) support deterministic replay/checkpointing for resumed streams. This ticket contains design decisions, example interfaces per language, test plan, rollout steps, and follow-ups for runtime and console telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: TypeScript SDK exposes a stable EventEmitter+typed envelope adapter that emits tokens, structured chunks, and tool-call lifecycle events
Python SDK exposes an async generator that yields typed events (token, structured, tool_call_start, tool_call_result, error) and supports checkpoint resume via idempotency token
Go SDK provides a channel-based StreamEvent abstraction with helper utilities to marshal/unwrap structured outputs and replay boundaries
Backward-compatible adapter layer converts legacy generator outputs to the new framed envelope format without changing public method signatures for key customer surface area
End-to-end e2e test covering tool call handshake, error retry, and resume scenarios (including a synthetic slow-network test)
Documentation and small migration guide snippets for TS/Python/Go included in the PR
tasks: Design envelope schema extension for tool-call lifecycle (fields: event_type, event_id, parent_id?, payload, seq, resume_token?)
Implement TS facade (EventEmitter) + adapter from legacy generator interface
Implement Python facade (async generator) + adapter function for legacy sync/generator clients
Implement Go facade (chan StreamEvent) + helper APIs for structured decode/ack
Add unit tests for framing, structured-output extraction, and idempotent replay
Integrate runtime framing change RFC (small non-breaking addition) and validate with canary hosts
Create docs/migration guide and code examples for each language
Instrument telemetry: per-event size, tool-call latencies, resume-rate, and error modes

implementation_notes: TS pattern: EventEmitter wrapper around low-level framed websocket/stream API. Example signature: class StreamSession extends EventEmitter { constructor(req) {}; close(): Promise<void>; /* emits: 'token'(string), 'structured'(object), 'tool:start'({id,name,args}), 'tool:result'({id,result}), 'error'({code,msg}) */ }
TS adapter example: function adapterFromLegacy(generatorFn) { return new StreamSession that pulls from the generator and emits framed envelopes; exposes same top-level .invoke API for compatibility.

Python pattern: async def stream_call(req) -> AsyncGenerator[Dict, None]: yields { 'type': 'token'|'structured'|'tool:start'|'tool:result'|'error', 'seq': int, 'resume_token': str|None, 'payload': ... }

Python adapter: def legacy_to_async(gen): wraps sync generator into an async generator by running on threadpool and emitting envelopes. Provide helper 'resume_from(token)' to rehydrate state until resume boundary.

Go pattern: type StreamEvent struct { Type string; Seq int64; ResumeToken string; Payload json.RawMessage } func InvokeStream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan StreamEvent, <-chan error) — consumer ranges over the events channel.
Go adapter: Provide SmallCompatibilityBridge that accepts legacy callback signature and translates callbacks into StreamEvent objects; include Close/Cancel semantics to avoid goroutine leaks.

Compatibility rules: adapters must not change public method names for existing top-level convenience APIs. New event envelope shapes guarded by sdkConfig.compatMode = 'sessionless-framed-v1' (default off until GA).
Telemetry: add 'stream_envelope_count', 'stream_resume_rate', 'tool_call_success_rate', and 'adapter_cpu_ns' metrics. Surface in Console under per-route streaming diagnostics tab.
Perf constraints: ensure per-token overhead < 50ns on fast paths; leverage zero-copy decoding when payloads are plain text tokens; benchmarked on dedicated-rt canaries.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Runtime change for resume_token emission could cause partial compatibility issues with older clients. Mitigation: make resume_token optional and only used when client opt-in; runtime supports both framed and legacy stream shapes for grace period.

Risk: Adapter adds CPU/latency overhead on high qps paths. Mitigation: provide zero-allocation fast-path in TS/Go where structured parsing is deferred until listener asks for it; add opt-out config for minimal-overhead binary streams.

Risk: Tool-call idempotency when replaying streams. Mitigation: include event_id + parent_id and require tool integration to be idempotent by default; document replay semantics and provide helper wrappers for common tools (http fetch, database writes).
Risk: API surface creep across languages leading to inconsistent ergonomics. Mitigation: centralize canonical examples in the design doc and run cross-language reviews with SDK owners before GA.
Risk: Backporting to legacy customers. Mitigation: provide migration guide and an experimental 'compatMode' flag; communicate via release notes and SDK changelogs.
